cohort: 222 pregnant women divided into two groups: teenage pregnancies (13-19 years, n=111) and adult pregnancies (20-29 years, n=111).
finding: Teenage mothers had a higher risk of anemia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, preterm delivery, low birth weight, cesarean delivery, and instrumental delivery compared to adult mothers.
mod_finding: Teenage mothers had higher rates of cesarean delivery (29.7% vs 14.4%) and instrumental vaginal delivery (8.1% vs 6.3%) compared to adult mothers.
gest_age: 37.6 weeks for teenagers and 38.95 weeks for adults
birth_weight: Low birth weight was observed in 18% of teenage pregnancies and 9% of adult pregnancies.
